original_card.question: Does one quantified step of the proposed #4100 all-size construction hold at its actual caller?
methods: Prove one missing implication with explicit quantified hypotheses.
Find an exact counterexample at the claimed interface boundary.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Identify the proposition and what would change downstream; do not equate a finite replay with a universal proof.

first_step.inspect: Read PROOF.md and AUDIT.md in #4100. Select one distinct obligation: CRT total repair, native/free-algebra lifting, precision/conditioning, or complete fixed-tape cost. This is an author-submitted proof, not an accepted unconditional theorem.
first_step.scope: Source-binding orientation only; no scientific replay, theorem acceptance or supplier admission. Budget any heavy replay separately.

original_card.first_experiment: Check live handoffs; name one proposition, its caller, quantified domain and dependency closure. Independently prove the implication or exhibit a precise gap/counterexample. Prioritize CRT.md total repair or COMPLEX.md free-algebra lift only if unclaimed. Stop at the chosen obligation; do not substitute finite samples or root arithmetic for an all-size proof, or launch the complete package by default.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Finite supplier improvements are useful only under the retained transfer obligations.
allowed_variations: One CRT repair, native lift, precision/conditioning or tape-cost proposition, with its exact caller.
scope_change_triggers: Replacing a quantified obligation with another finite smoke test.
Treating archive intake, an author PASS receipt or a finite composed fixture as discharge of the universal hypotheses.

existing_checks.scope: PR #4100: proposed unconditional construction and finite checks, without independent acceptance.
existing_checks.remaining: Independent proof audit of one caller-bound all-size implication; all other premises remain explicit.

actual_scope: Audit the tape-level head accounting (section 2.3) and variable-length lockstep transpose (step 4) of #4100's vendor/UNION-SCHEDULE.md with a per-pass written accounting and an exact-integer multitape simulation of the whole schedule.
scope_change_reason: The card asks for one quantified implication at its caller; this is the fixed-tape cost of the per-visit union movement row, which the source and the PR2578 review both leave unreviewed at tape level.
bottleneck_link: The union row has slack about 0.406 in #4100's ledger; an extra factor g=p^beta or L=poly(p) in head travel would exhaust it and invalidate the proposed exponent.
stop_rule: Stop once the per-round head travel is bounded with explicit constants and matched by literal head counts with failing controls.
evidence: README per-pass accounting: union movement <= sum_r |S_r| [(15nb+16lev+17)RW + 4nb+4]; verify.py: six exact cases (g=3..6, V up to 16,807) reproduce the Kronecker product, every extracted group is a complete E_f-line, union head travel <= 0.989 of the bound and 13.5-15.9 x RW sum|F| (nb+lev+1) across 3-6 rounds; controls: dropped round and mismatched zip chunks detected, stale rewinds exceed the bound (2.6x sparse, 1.66x dense), old per-axis scan visits 3.44 sum|F|.
author: Ryanson Jonathan, with Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5) assistance
ai_assistance: Substantial Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5) assistance in reading, accounting proof, simulator implementation and writing; no independent human or proof-kernel review.

open_questions.question: Charge the batched boundary arithmetic's row-field movement on the same tape model.
open_questions.why_it_matters: This audit counts the line sweep conservatively inside the union total; #4100 charges batched right-hand sides to the boundary row with only the polynomial-width row field moved.
open_questions.first_step: Add a batch tape and count row-field moves per batch of lines of width W to 2W.

open_questions.question: Bind the header width (flags, coordinates, ordinal) to #4100's actual record format.
open_questions.why_it_matters: The accounting assumes O(g log L)-bit headers, i.e. o(p).
open_questions.first_step: Fix the header layout and check g log L = o(p) against #4100's beta and core side L.
